answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that vests slowly, like quartz forming under pressure: creating one identity is cheap, but creating thousands ties up capital for months. Honest work then builds a spiral of verifiable reputation, completed jobs, peer reviews, and on-time delivery, that cannot be transferred to a fresh account. Like a cedar that takes years to grow tall, reputation is earned over time, so an attacker who burns a fake identity loses both its stake and its history, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
